forecasts.question: Will Iran resume negotiations with the US before EOD 2026-06-16?

No publicly confirmed held session between named US-Iranian envoys nor formal MFA rescission of the June 1 suspension occurred before EOD June 16. Written-message exchanges resolve AMBIGUOUS-NO per criteria. Lucerne round-1 (June 21-22) was the first held session but missed the window.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if, before EOD 2026-06-16, a publicly confirmed HELD negotiating session (direct or mediated via Oman/Qatar/Pakistan) occurs between named US and Iranian principals/envoys, OR an official Iranian statement (MFA/state media IRNA/Tasnim/Fars) rescinds the 2026-06-01 suspension. A held mediated session counts; mere rhetorical assertion that 'talks continue' or relay of written messages does NOT count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two independent TIER1 OR one TIER1 + official Iranian state-media; State Dept or Iran MFA statement also resolves.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Trump-only assertions without Iranian/mediator confirmation do NOT count; written-message exchanges that are not a convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO; one side asserting talks 'continue' without a named convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

forecasts.question: Will Hormuz reach >=50 commercial transits/day (7-day avg) before EOD 2026-07-02?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO. Post-MOU recovery peaked at 51-52 single-day transits (June 24-25) but the 7-day rolling average never reached 50 in any window before July 2. CNN Business (June 26): approximately 25 ships/day in late June. SP Global (June 24): tanker traffic dipping. July 9 ceasefire collapse and resumed strikes ended even the modest recovery. The 7-day average requirement could not be satisfied by two peak days embedded in a lower-traffic window.

forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Naval-escorted convoys count; one-off surge days below a 7-day window do NOT qualify; if PortWatch unpublished, use best AIS tracker and flag AMBIGUOUS if sources conflict >20%.

forecasts.question: Will the Knesset pass the dissolution bill's final reading with a fixed election date earlier than 2026-10-27 before EOD 2026-07-15?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO. Both resolution conditions fail independently. (1) Deadline: final reading passed July 17 — two days after the July 15 deadline. (2) Election date: October 27, 2026, which is not earlier than October 27 (it is precisely October 27). The coalition's own dissolution bill — though ultimately successful — was slower than forecast (first reading June 2 to final reading July 17 = 45 days), and converged on the constitutional deadline date rather than an earlier one.

forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Preliminary/first/second readings without final passage do NOT count; passage that leaves the date to a later committee or sets only a band without a fixed date = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO; if a fixed date on/after 27 Oct is set, resolve NO.

forecasts.question: Will the United States and Iran publicly confirm a mutual ceasefire or halt-in-place before EOD 2026-07-28?
forecasts.delta_reason: As of July 25, both sides are publicly opposed to an immediate ceasefire. Trump told reporters July 24: 'they need more of the same,' while also calling Iran 'getting more serious.' Iranian officials formally rejected the Iraqi PM's ceasefire proposal, citing unresolved Hormuz governance. Qatar and Pakistan floated a 10-day ceasefire proposal (July 20) that neither side has accepted. The US is conducting its 13th+ consecutive night of strikes. The June 17 MOU precedent (suspension resolved in 16 days) is noted, but the July 9 collapse occurred in a more kinetic environment. The 0.10 floor reflects that rapid diplomatic reversals have occurred in this conflict but current signals show no imminent turn.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if named US officials AND named Iranian officials (or a named mediator on behalf of both) publicly confirm a mutual halt in offensive military strikes, specifying a start date and both sides affirming. Both sides must confirm. Duration irrelevant.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: TIER1 outlet (CNN, Reuters, BBC, AP, Al Jazeera, Axios) reporting both sides confirming the halt. State-media-only announcement without US confirmation = AMBIGUOUS.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Unilateral US pause not confirmed by Iran = AMBIGUOUS-NO. Iranian announcement not confirmed by any US official within 6 hours = AMBIGUOUS-NO. Mediator press conference not confirmed by both governments = AMBIGUOUS-NO.

indicators.name: Trump public ceasefire statement or offer
indicators.expected_effect: A Trump statement offering or accepting ceasefire is the primary leading indicator; current CONTRADICTED by 'they need more of the same'

indicators.expected_effect: Iranian rejection of Iraqi PM proposal is CONTRADICTED; reversal would move p +20pp

indicators.expected_effect: 10-day proposal floated July 20 but not accepted; announcement of acceptance would trigger YES

forecasts.question: Will Mojtaba Khamenei make a verified public appearance (confirmed live video or authenticated photograph showing his face) before EOD 2026-08-08?
forecasts.delta_reason: Mojtaba Khamenei has not made a public appearance since assuming the role of Supreme Leader on March 8, 2026 — 139 days as of July 25. He communicates exclusively through written statements read on state television. Iranian state media has increasingly prefaced his name with the title 'Ayatollah' — a title he did not hold at appointment and that requires formal clerical conferral. Fox News cited sources describing him as 'misfunctioning, not controlling regime.' His absence during the July 4-9 Ali Khamenei funeral procession (despite strong political incentive to appear) is strong negative evidence. A public appearance would carry substantial legitimacy value for the regime but the security risk during active US strikes is real.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if at least one TIER1 outlet independently verifies a video or photograph showing Mojtaba Khamenei's face in a live or dated setting after 2026-07-25. State-media-released video must be independently authenticated. Written statements or audio-only releases = RESOLVE-NO.

forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If a video is released by Iranian state media but its date cannot be authenticated as post-July-25, resolve AMBIGUOUS (count as NO). Blurred or partial-face images where identification is disputed = RESOLVE-NO.

forecasts.question: Will Houthi forces publicly claim and execute at least 3 additional confirmed strikes on commercial or Saudi-flagged maritime vessels in the Red Sea, Gulf of Aden, or Bab el-Mandeb before EOD 2026-08-04?
forecasts.delta_reason: Houthis declared a formal naval blockade against Saudi, Israeli, and US-linked shipping on July 23, 2026, and struck two Saudi oil tankers the same day (setting one ablaze). This is the first time the group has named Saudi Arabia as an explicit blockade target. Saudi Arabia conducted counter-strikes on Houthi territory July 23. The Houthis have not voluntarily suspended maritime attacks for more than 5 consecutive days in 2026. Historical pattern: Saudi counter-strikes are followed by Houthi maritime acceleration. UKMTO Red Sea threat level at CRITICAL as of July 23.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if at least 3 separate Houthi-claimed maritime strikes on commercial, tanker, or Saudi-flagged vessels occur after 2026-07-25 and before EOD 2026-08-04, each confirmed by at least one TIER1 or OSINT shipping-monitor source. Only attacks on non-military vessels count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: UKMTO, Ambrey Analytics, UANI shipping monitor, or TIER1 wire services confirming attacks. Houthi claim alone without damage report or third-party confirmation = AMBIGUOUS for that individual strike.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If fewer than 3 attacks are confirmed by TIER1 sources but Houthis claim ≥3 and no independent denial exists, resolve AMBIGUOUS (count as YES given track record). If Saudi Arabia or UN declares a blockade deal that Houthis verifiably honor, resolve NO regardless of prior attacks in window.

forecasts.question: Will Brent crude oil close above $110/barrel on any single trading day before EOD 2026-08-08?
forecasts.delta_reason: Brent closed at $101.10 on July 23 after the Houthi Saudi tanker attacks — first close above $100 since late May. Retreated to $97-98 on July 24. The dual chokepoint problem (Hormuz near-closed, Red Sea under Houthi blockade) constrains approximately 30-35% of seaborne oil globally. Goldman Sachs forecast $120/barrel by Q4 2026 if disruptions continue. However, a further $9-10 gain requires either a major Hormuz escalation event or prolonged Saudi shipping disruption; the US has released SPR stocks throughout the conflict. The 0.42 probability reflects the elevated baseline ($101 ceiling tested) against the SPR buffer and the 14-day window constraint.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Brent crude ICE front-month futures close at or above $110.00/barrel on any single trading day between 2026-07-25 and 2026-08-08 inclusive. Intraday spikes that do not survive the close = RESOLVE-NO.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: ICE exchange settlement data or Bloomberg/Reuters closing price confirmation. Any TIER1 financial outlet reporting the day's closing Brent price ≥ $110.00 = sufficient.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If markets are halted by circuit breakers and the last confirmed price was ≥$110, resolve AMBIGUOUS (count as YES). If the Brent contract rolls to a new front month during the period, use the new front-month contract.

forecasts.question: Will the IAEA publicly confirm that its inspection team has physically entered Iran and begun verification activities at at least one declared Iranian nuclear facility before 2026-09-15?
forecasts.delta_reason: IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi stated on July 25, 2026 that Iran has invited an IAEA inspection team to visit 'within weeks' — the first such invitation since IAEA inspectors withdrew during the early conflict. This is a fresh datapoint on the day of this report's creation. However, Iran has previously extended IAEA invitations and then cancelled or restricted delegations; the active US bombing campaign and MOU collapse create a volatile environment in which Iran may use the invitation as diplomatic leverage without following through on site access. The 0.35 probability reflects a real development against a track record of Iranian inspection access management.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if IAEA Director General or official spokesperson states in a public communication that IAEA inspectors physically entered Iran and conducted or commenced at least one monitoring or verification visit at a facility covered under Iran's Comprehensive Safeguards Agreement before 2026-09-15. YES applies even if inspectors are subsequently expelled, provided at least one site visit commenced.

A single 'goodwill visit' with camera access at a facility gate without entry to monitoring instruments = AMBIGUOUS-NO.

forecasts.question: Will the United States and Iran sign a formally documented ceasefire agreement (or mutually confirmed interim deal) before EOD 2026-10-01?
forecasts.delta_reason: The conflict has cycled through two ceasefire-then-collapse sequences (April 8 ceasefire, June 17 MOU). Both sides have demonstrated willingness to negotiate but Hormuz governance and Iran's nuclear program remain irresolvable in short windows. As of July 25: 13+ consecutive nights of US strikes; Iran rejected Iraqi PM proposal; mediators floated a 10-day ceasefire not accepted by either side; Brent at $101. The 68-day window through Oct 1 allows time for accumulated economic and military pressure on both sides to drive a third ceasefire attempt. The June 1 suspension resolved in 16 days (June 17 MOU) as a precedent for rapid reversals. Active mediator engagement (Qatar, Pakistan, potentially Oman) maintains the structural prerequisites.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a formal written ceasefire agreement or interim deal is signed by named US and Iranian representatives (or publicly acknowledged in joint statement by named mediator hosting both sides), with both sides confirming cessation of offensive strikes. A repeat of the June 17 MOU format — both sides acknowledging the same document with named mediator — qualifies. A unilateral pause does not qualify.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: TIER1 outlet publishing the text or terms of the agreement with attribution to named US and Iranian officials. Qatar FM, Pakistan PM, or Oman FM confirming the signing as named mediator = sufficient.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If fighting stops for ≥5 days but no document is signed, resolve AMBIGUOUS (count as NO — the question requires formal documentation). If one side claims an agreement and the other denies it, resolve NO.

forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu's Likud-led bloc win sufficient seats to form a governing coalition in the October 27, 2026 Israeli legislative election?
forecasts.delta_reason: Current polling (Channel 13, July 2026) places the Netanyahu bloc at approximately 51 seats versus 58 for the center-left opposition — 10 short of the 61-seat majority. A Chatham House analysis published July 2026 described the Iran war as having 'failed to deliver the decisive victory many Israelis expected.' Netanyahu's corruption trial resumes after the election. The anti-Netanyahu bloc's path to 61 seats depends on Arab party participation (without them, estimated at 59 seats). Security conditions could produce a late rally effect for Netanyahu. The 0.32 probability reflects a real but below-even chance for the Netanyahu bloc, consistent with both sides' published polling and the Arab party dependency the opposition faces.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if (a) official Israeli Central Elections Committee results show Netanyahu's bloc (Likud and all coalition partners) at ≥61 seats AND (b) Netanyahu is formally designated as PM-elect by the Israeli president before EOD 2026-11-30.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Israeli Central Elections Committee official preliminary results for seat count; Israeli President's formal designation announcement for PM designation. TIER1 Israeli outlets (Haaretz, Times of Israel, Ynet) projections used for initial resolution pending official count.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If Netanyahu's bloc reaches 61 seats but a coalition is not formed within the standard 28-day formation window, resolve AMBIGUOUS (count as YES on the seat criterion — question is about winning sufficient seats). If elections are postponed beyond Oct 27 due to war emergency, resolve AMBIGUOUS (count as NO).
